identifiers.title: Randomized controlled trial for time-restricted eating in healthy volunteers without obesity
identifiers.authors: Xie Z, Sun Y, Ye Y, Hu D, Zhang H, He Z, Zhao H, Yang H, Mao Y
identifiers.citation: Xie Z, Sun Y, Ye Y, Hu D, Zhang H, He Z, Zhao H, Yang H, Mao Y. Randomized controlled trial for time-restricted eating in healthy volunteers without obesity. Nat Commun. 2022;13. doi:10.1038/s41467-022-28662-5

design.quote: Ninety participants were randomized to eTRF (n=30), mTRF (n=30), or control groups (n=30) using a computer-based random-number generator.

species.quote: Ninety participants were randomized to eTRF (n=30), mTRF (n=30), or control groups (n=30) using a computer-based random-number generator.

population.quote: We conducted a five-week randomized trial to compare the effects of the two TRF regimens in healthy individuals without obesity (ChiCTR2000029797).

sampleSize.quote: Remaining 82 participants completed the trial and were included in the present analysis.

facts.label: Early group: an 8-hour eating window between 6:00 and 15:00
facts.value: eating during no more than 8 h between 06:00 and 15:00
facts.quote: We conducted a randomized, controlled trial, in which participants were randomized to an eTRF group (eating during no more than 8 h between 06:00 and 15:00 and fasting for the rest of the day), an mTRF group (eating during no more than 8 h between 11:00 and 20:00 and fasting for the rest of the day), and a control group (eating ad libitum over 8 h each day).

facts.label: Mid-day group: an 8-hour eating window between 11:00 and 20:00
facts.value: eating during no more than 8 h between 11:00 and 20:00
facts.quote: We conducted a randomized, controlled trial, in which participants were randomized to an eTRF group (eating during no more than 8 h between 06:00 and 15:00 and fasting for the rest of the day), an mTRF group (eating during no more than 8 h between 11:00 and 20:00 and fasting for the rest of the day), and a control group (eating ad libitum over 8 h each day).

facts.label: Control group: ate as usual, over more than 8 hours a day
facts.value: eating ad libitum over 8 h each day
facts.quote: We conducted a randomized, controlled trial, in which participants were randomized to an eTRF group (eating during no more than 8 h between 06:00 and 15:00 and fasting for the rest of the day), an mTRF group (eating during no more than 8 h between 11:00 and 20:00 and fasting for the rest of the day), and a control group (eating ad libitum over 8 h each day).

facts.label: The early group picked its own 8 hours inside 6:00 to 15:00
facts.value: choose an 8 h eating period between 6:00 and 15:00
facts.quote: Participants in the eTRF group were instructed to choose an 8 h eating period between 6:00 and 15:00 and to fast for the rest of the day.

facts.label: The mid-day group picked its own 8 hours inside 11:00 to 20:00
facts.value: choose an 8 h eating period between 11:00 and 20:00
facts.quote: Those in mTRF group were instructed to choose an 8 h eating period between 11:00 and 20:00 and to fast for the rest of the day.

facts.label: The control group kept its usual eating
facts.quote: Participants in the control group could eat ad libitum, following their usual eating regimens, with food being consumed over more than 8 h per day.

facts.label: Allowed while fasting: water, sparkling water, unsweetened tea, coffee
facts.value: water, flavored carbonated water, unsweetened tea, and coffee
facts.quote: Participants in the eTRF and mTRF groups were only allowed to consume water, flavored carbonated water, unsweetened tea, and coffee during the fasting period.

facts.label: No diet: both eating-window groups ate what they liked within their hours
facts.value: no specific nutritional guidance was given to them
facts.quote: The participants in both TRF groups were instructed to eat ad libitum during their daily 8 h eating periods and no specific nutritional guidance was given to them, such that the trial conditions were similar to real-life situations.

facts.label: Length of the trial
facts.quote: We conducted a five-week randomized trial to compare the effects of the two TRF regimens in healthy individuals without obesity (ChiCTR2000029797).

facts.label: Groups set by a computer's random numbers
facts.quote: Ninety participants were randomized to eTRF (n=30), mTRF (n=30), or control groups (n=30) using a computer-based random-number generator.

facts.label: Main outcome: change in insulin resistance (HOMA-IR, from fasting glucose and insulin)
facts.quote: The primary outcome was the change in HOMA-IR, an index of insulin resistance that is calculated using the fasting glucose and insulin concentrations.

facts.label: Other outcomes
facts.value: energy intake, fasting glucose, body mass, body composition
facts.quote: The secondary outcomes were changes in energy intake, fasting glucose, body mass, body composition, blood pressure, blood lipid concentrations, inflammatory markers, liver enzymes, immune cells, gut microbiota, sleep quality, and appetite.

facts.label: Daily-rhythm measures were exploratory
facts.quote: Change in daily rhythms of plasma adipokine concentrations and PBMC clock gene expression were measured as exploratory analyses.

facts.label: Registered before anyone enrolled
facts.quote: Prior to enrolling participants, the study was registered at chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2000029797).

facts.label: Recruited in the Beijing area, February to March 2020
facts.quote: Participants were recruited from the Beijing area from Feb. 16th, 2020, to Mar. 22nd, 2020, by means of posters, emails, flyers, social media, and website advertisements.

facts.label: Everyone usually ate over more than 8 hours a day and had not fasted recently
facts.value: in the habit of eating over more than 8 h per day
facts.quote: Ninety participants who were in the habit of eating over more than 8 h per day and who did not have recent experience of fasting were recruited into the trial after providing their written informed consent.

facts.label: Who could join: aged 18 to 64
facts.quote: The inclusion criteria were: (1) 18–64 years old; (2) ability to attend the hospital at regular intervals; (3) ability to independently provide informed consent; (4) BMI between 17.5 and 30.0 kg/m2; (5) daily feeding period of more than 8 h; and (6) stable body mass (change < ±10% of current body mass during the 3 months prior to the study).

facts.label: Who could join: BMI 17.5 to 30.0
facts.quote: The inclusion criteria were: (1) 18–64 years old; (2) ability to attend the hospital at regular intervals; (3) ability to independently provide informed consent; (4) BMI between 17.5 and 30.0 kg/m2; (5) daily feeding period of more than 8 h; and (6) stable body mass (change < ±10% of current body mass during the 3 months prior to the study).

facts.label: Who was excluded: night shifts, recent fasting, diabetes, high blood pressure and more
facts.value: a diagnosis of hypertension, diabetes, or other metabolic disease
facts.quote: The exclusion criteria were: (1) night-shift work more than once a week; (2) fasting during the preceding 8 weeks; (3) alcohol consumption more than twice a week; (4) pregnancy, gastrointestinal abnormalities or eating disorders, history of gastrointestinal surgery or systemic disease; (5) use of corticosteroid drugs, β-receptor blockers, or other drugs that might affect the findings; (6) a diagnosis of hypertension, diabetes, or other metabolic disease; and (7) a diagnosis of insomnia.

facts.label: Excluded: night shifts more than once a week
facts.value: night-shift work more than once a week
facts.quote: The exclusion criteria were: (1) night-shift work more than once a week; (2) fasting during the preceding 8 weeks; (3) alcohol consumption more than twice a week; (4) pregnancy, gastrointestinal abnormalities or eating disorders, history of gastrointestinal surgery or systemic disease; (5) use of corticosteroid drugs, β-receptor blockers, or other drugs that might affect the findings; (6) a diagnosis of hypertension, diabetes, or other metabolic disease; and (7) a diagnosis of insomnia.

facts.label: Alcohol kept at the usual level, no more than twice a week
facts.value: no more than twice a week
facts.quote: The participants maintained their habitual alcohol intake during the trial, which was no more than twice a week, as required in the eligibility criteria.

facts.label: Everyone photographed each meal at its start and end
facts.value: take photos of their food as they began to eat and as they finished
facts.quote: To ensure compliance, participants were required to take photos of their food as they began to eat and as they finished and to send them privately to the investigators using a WeChat-supported web message-sending applet.

facts.label: Food energy was estimated from the meal photos
facts.value: Energy intake was estimated using pictures of the meals consumed
facts.quote: Energy intake was estimated using pictures of the meals consumed.

facts.label: The researchers who estimated food from photos knew each person's group
facts.value: were not blinded to the assignment of the group
facts.quote: Investigators who checked posted photos and estimated energy contents from photos were not blinded to the assignment of the group.

facts.label: Participants knew their group
facts.value: they were not blinded to the assignment of the groups
facts.quote: Because participants were instructed to take either TRF regimen or normal diet regimen, they were not blinded to the assignment of the groups.

facts.label: The researchers who measured outcomes did not know the groups
facts.value: Researchers who assessed the outcomes were blinded to group assignment
facts.quote: Researchers who assessed the outcomes were blinded to group assignment, but participants and care givers were not.

facts.label: Body fat measured by a bioelectrical impedance scale
facts.quote: Body mass and percentage body fat were measured using an HBF-371 Bioelectrical impedance analyzer (Omron Healthcare Co., Kyoto, Japan).

facts.label: Blood taken in the morning after at least 8 hours' fast
facts.value: after an overnight fast of at least 8 h
facts.quote: Fasting blood sampled were collected during the morning (07:00–08:30) after an overnight fast of at least 8 h.

facts.label: Planned: 22 finishers a group needed, 30 recruited
facts.value: 22 participants would have to complete the trial in each group
facts.quote: Therefore, to detect a 37.5% difference in HOMA-IR (1.91 × 0.375 = 0.7) between the TRF groups, the statistical power analysis indicated that 22 participants would have to complete the trial in each group in order to achieve 80% power (two-sided test, a = 0.05), assuming a within-participants standard deviation of 0.8.

facts.label: 30 recruited per group
facts.value: 30 participants were recruited for each group
facts.quote: Taking into consideration potential drop-outs during the trial, 30 participants were recruited for each group.

facts.label: The eight who did not finish were left out of the analysis
facts.quote: The energy that was consumed on non-compliant days was not included in the calculation of the mean daily energy consumption and the data for the eight participants who did not complete the trial were excluded from the analyses.

facts.label: Why eight dropped out
facts.value: dissatisfaction with the randomization result or for personal scheduling conflicts
facts.quote: During the 5-week intervention, eight participants (eTRF: n = 2; mTRF: n = 4; control: n = 2) dropped out due to dissatisfaction with the randomization result or for personal scheduling conflicts.

facts.label: 429 people screened
facts.quote: A total of 429 individuals were assessed for eligibility and 312 were excluded as they did not meet inclusion criteria, and 17 were excluded as they declined to participate.

facts.label: 82 finished and were analysed
facts.quote: Remaining 82 participants completed the trial and were included in the present analysis.

facts.label: Daily-rhythm blood samples came from 19 people, at four times of day
facts.quote: Furthermore, blood samples were collected at four times of day (07:00, 12:00, 17:00, and 23:00) at both the beginning and end of the interventions from 19 participants (five, eight, and six from the eTRF, mTRF, and control groups, respectively).

facts.label: Who paid for the study
facts.value: CAMS Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences (CIFMS)
facts.quote: This work was supported by grants from the CAMS Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences (CIFMS) (No.2016-I2M-1-001) (Y.M. and H.Y.).

facts.label: The funder had no role in the study
facts.quote: The study sponsors played no role in study design, conduct, data acquisition, analysis, manuscript preparation or the decision to submit the manuscript for publication.

facts.label: Competing interests
facts.quote: The authors declare no competing interests.

facts.label: People said they kept to their window on almost every day
facts.quote: Self-reported compliance with the regimens was 949 out of 980 person-days (96.8%) in the eTRF group, and 894 out of 910 person-days (98.2%) in the mTRF group.
facts.outcome: Days kept to the eating window (self-reported)

facts.label: Mid-day group kept to its window on 98.2% of days (self-reported)

facts.outcome: Days kept to the eating window (self-reported)

facts.label: Both eating-window groups ate less than the control group
facts.quote: There was a significant difference in the change in energy intake among the eTRF, mTRF, and control groups (p < 0.001), with the eTRF (Δ = −240 ± 409 kcal/day) and mTRF (Δ = −159 ± 397 kcal/day) groups showing a reduction in energy intake, whereas the control group (Δ = 64 ± 286 kcal/day; p < 0.001 and p < 0.01, respectively) did not.
facts.outcome: Change in food energy eaten per day

facts.label: Insulin resistance changed differently across the groups
facts.quote: There were significantly different changes in the Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR) among the groups (ANOVA p < 0.001, Fig. 2b).
facts.outcome: Change in insulin resistance (HOMA-IR)

facts.label: Time-restricted eating limits eating to 4 to 10 hours a day
facts.value: restricted to a period of 4–10 h
facts.quote: Time-restricted feeding (TRF), in which the daily window for food consumption is restricted to a period of 4–10 h, is thought to be a feasible fasting regimen for most people.

facts.label: Earlier work in animals found many benefits
facts.quote: It has previously been shown in animal models that TRF has many beneficial effects, including a reduction in body mass, the prevention of obesity, an improvement in insulin sensitivity, a reduction in hepatic fat content, the prevention of hepatosteatosis and hyperlipidemia, and the amelioration of hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury and inflammation–.

facts.label: Earlier work in people found weight loss and better insulin response
facts.quote: TRF has also been shown to induce weight loss, increase insulin sensitivity, and reduce blood pressure, and to have other metabolic benefits in humans,–.

facts.label: Earlier work suggests the timing of the window matters
facts.value: might depend on the particular time window
facts.quote: Previous studies have shown that the effects of TRF might depend on the particular time window for food consumption, but the exact time periods used to date have not been well defined.

facts.label: Authors' suggestion: the mechanism may involve daily rhythms
facts.value: the mechanism may involve changes to daily rhythms
facts.quote: Taken together, these findings suggest that TRF with a window for food consumption early in the day is better for metabolic health than a window later in the day, and that the mechanism may involve changes to daily rhythms.

facts.label: Authors' reading: the two windows' different results were not from eating different amounts
facts.value: were not caused by differences in energy intake
facts.quote: Furthermore, the lack of a significant difference in the change in energy intake between the two TRF groups suggests that the differences in the improvements in metabolic health were not caused by differences in energy intake.

facts.label: Authors' reading: shortening the eating day alone cut how much people ate
facts.value: energy intake can be limited just by shortening the daily duration of food consumption
facts.quote: However, there were reductions in energy intake in both of the TRF groups, which implies that energy intake can be limited just by shortening the daily duration of food consumption.

facts.label: Weight loss was modest against earlier studies of people with overweight
facts.quote: Besides, the weight loss in eTRF group was relatively modest compared with prior eTRF studies,, which may be the result of different inclusion criteria of participants, with normal weight humans included in this trial, while mostly overweight participants or individuals with obesity were included in prior eTRF studies,.

facts.label: An earlier trial in people with higher blood pressure found it fell
facts.quote: The baseline blood pressure levels might be the reason for the different effects of eTRF between these two trials, because the trial by Courtney Peterson et al. was carried on those with a mean blood pressure within prehypertensive range, while the present trial on healthy participants.

facts.label: Blood fats were already in the normal range for most
facts.quote: In addition, there was no effect of either TRF regimen on circulating lipid concentrations, but this was not unexpected, because the blood concentrations of most of the participants were within the normal range.

facts.label: Authors' reading: higher ghrelin at 23:00 may simply reflect a longer fast by then
facts.value: a longer period of fasting in this group at that time point
facts.quote: Therefore, the higher concentration of ghrelin that was identified at 23:00 in the eTRF group might be at least in part the results of a longer period of fasting in this group at that time point.

facts.label: Ghrelin plays a role in feeling hungry
facts.value: ghrelin has an important role in the feeling of hunger
facts.quote: The daily rhythm in circulating ghrelin concentration has been reported to synchronize with TRF in mice, with the concentration increasing before the feeding period, and it should be noted that ghrelin has an important role in the feeling of hunger.

facts.label: The body-clock gene results were exploratory only
facts.quote: Because not all the expression data for every participant fitted Cosinor curves, the parameters were calculated just for exploratory purposes, to provide clues for future investigations.

facts.label: Participants knew which group they were in
facts.value: the participants could not be blinded to the intervention
facts.quote: Firstly, although it was a randomized trial, the participants could not be blinded to the intervention.

facts.label: Volunteers may already have been keen on time-restricted eating, and most were women
facts.quote: Secondly, the people who applied to join the trial might already have been interested in TRF or wished to improve their health through making a dietary change, and most were women.

facts.label: Small trial, perhaps not representative
facts.value: the number of participants in the trial was relatively small
facts.quote: Thirdly, the number of participants in the trial was relatively small and they may not have been representative of the wider population.

facts.label: Barriers to keeping the window were not studied
facts.value: the potential barriers to TRF were not analyzed
facts.quote: Fourthly, the potential barriers to TRF were not analyzed.

facts.label: Meal timing and length varied within each group
facts.value: the specific timing and duration of their meals varied within each group
facts.quote: Fifthly, the participants in the TRF groups were required to consume their meals within an 8 h period, but the specific timing and duration of their meals varied within each group, which may have influenced the results.

facts.label: How the length of the window matters needs more study
facts.quote: The influence of the duration of food consumption on the effects of TRF requires further investigation.

facts.label: Fasting length before the blood tests may have differed between groups
facts.value: changes in the duration of fasting prior to testing
facts.quote: Sixthly, the changes in the eating periods that were made in the TRF groups may have caused changes in the duration of fasting prior to testing, which might have influenced the results.

facts.label: Daily-rhythm measures came from few people at few times
facts.value: measured in limited numbers of participants
facts.quote: Lastly, daily rhythm-related parameters were measured in limited numbers of participants and few time points were assessed.

facts.label: Larger rhythm studies are needed
facts.value: further, larger studies should be conducted
facts.quote: To better assess the effects of TRFs on daily rhythms, further, larger studies should be conducted that include shorter intervals between measurements and more than one diurnal cycle.

facts.label: Belly fat needs measuring in future trials
facts.value: requires further visceral fat measuring parameters in future trials
facts.quote: These may indicate an improvement in fat deposition, which requires further visceral fat measuring parameters in future trials.

facts.label: Food timing on the test day may have affected the rhythm results
facts.value: the timing of food intake on the test day might influence the results
facts.quote: However, it is worth noting that the timing of food intake on the test day might influence the results of the analyses of daily rhythm-related parameters.

facts.label: Five weeks only
facts.quote: The present study has shown that 5 weeks of eTRF, but not mTRF, improves insulin sensitivity, reduces fasting plasma glucose, reduces body mass and adiposity, ameliorates inflammation, and increases gut microbial diversity.
